title: Introduce prefill-decode arbiter with token-slip resolver to reduce tail latency in interleaved microbatches
author: Sofia Nguyen
commits: a1b2c3d: add arbiter core and token-slip resolver
d4e5f6a: integrate arbiter into microbatch scheduler
b7c8d9e: add unit and perf tests, docs and feature flag
description: Motivation: In high-concurrency interactive workloads we see tail latency caused by mismatch between prefill completion and decode pipeline admission (especially with interleaved microbatches and KV snapshots). This PR implements a lightweight prefill-decode arbiter and a token-slip resolver that together reduce tail amplification when prefill fragments finish out-of-order. Design summary: 1) Arbiter: a per-GPU token-budgeted admission controller that tracks inflight prefill fragments and decode lanes; it enforces a soft budget per microstripe and prioritizes decode admission based on token age, model priority, and observed KV readiness. 2) Token-slip resolver: when a prefill fragment finishes earlier or later than its paired decode window, the resolver computes a minimal token-alignment correction (slip) to avoid unnecessary decode stalls or duplicated KV priming. The resolver prefers KV reuse over redundant priming where safe. 3) Snapshotted KV hints: integrate a lightweight KV snapshot tag with prefill fragments to allow decode to select warm KV lanes without full re-prime. Implementation notes: arbiter implemented in runtime/scheduler/arbiter.py as ~250LOC modular component; it exposes a tiny admission API (request_admit, release_tokens, prioritize) and a metrics surface (arbiter.requests, arbiter.rejected, arbiter.slips). Token-slip resolver implemented in runtime/inference/pipeline.py and runtime/kv/kv_snapshotter.cc; it attaches a 64-bit snapshot tag to prefill responses and allows decode to consult tag->slot mapping before priming. Feature gated behind feature-flag "prefill_decode_arbiter" and rolled out under canary. Benchmarks: microbatch interleave workload (grp: chat-heavy, model: rw-7b, seq_len: 2048) shows p95 generation latency down 18% (from 412ms to 337ms), mean token throughput up 6%, and token CPU-equivalent cost down ~3% when arbiter enabled and snapshot reuse occurs. Tail scenarios with high KV churn show p99 improvement 11%. Tests: unit tests for arbiter logic, deterministic token-slip cases, and an integration perf harness that simulates out-of-order prefill completions. CI: added perf-check and a synthetic e2e streaming run; perf-check is run on a pinned hw node in CI. Compatibility/caveats: arbiter assumes decode kernels can accept a soft-aligned token window; some extremely latency-sensitive models with strict kernel tiling may need per-model opt-out. The KV snapshot tag is intentionally conservative to avoid stale reads; snapshot reuse is only allowed when model pins match and token prefix is deterministic. Rollout plan: 1) feature-flag canary on 5% of traffic for 72h, 2) expand to 25% with increased tracing and cost telemetry, 3) full rollout after 7d if regressions absent. Observability: new dashboards in Console: arbiter/admit-rate, arbiter/slip-count, kv/snapshot-reuse-rate and a per-model breakdown. Related work: builds on ENG-6492 (continuous-batching improvements) and complements earlier prefetch efforts; differs by focusing on admission arbitration and token-level alignment rather than kernel fusion. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] perf harness, [x] feature flag, [x] docs, [x] canary plan, [x] rollout observability. Requests for reviewers: sanity-check admission fairness under synthetic skew, validate snapshot correctness for non-deterministic prefix transforms, confirm perf numbers on internal bench farm.
review_thread: Aisha Khan: This looks promising, can the arbiter starvation-proof lower-priority lanes?
Sofia Nguyen: Arbiter implements an aging counter; lower-priority lanes get guaranteed progress after 100ms of waiting (configurable).
Marco Li: Can the token-slip resolver cause duplicated KV primes in edge cases?

Sofia Nguyen: The resolver checks snapshot tag + model pin; duplication is possible only when model config differs mid-request, which we explicitly disallow — added assert and a metric to catch regressions.
Elena Roberts: CI perf-check failed initially on the pinned node (no GPU), why?
Sofia Nguyen: Initial CI job attempted to run on a non-pinned runner; fixed perf-check workflow to use gpu-pinned executor, rerun passed.
Aisha Khan: Approve after minor doc clarifications
release_notes: Introduce prefill-decode arbiter and token-slip resolver to reduce tail latency for interleaved microbatch workloads; feature gated (prefill_decode_arbiter) and canaried. Improves p95 latency ~18% on chat-heavy benchmarks.
